name: Tallahassee
summary: Florida's capital in the rolling, oak-canopied hills of the panhandle — an old-and-new capitol, a big university, and a reconstructed Spanish mission.

foodMustTry.name: Apalachicola oysters
foodMustTry.blurb: Some of the Gulf's best, from just down the coast.

days.label: Day 244 — The Capital & the Canopy Roads
days.summary: Two capitols and a Spanish mission.

item.title: Florida State Capitol & the Old Capitol
item.blurb: The tall modern capitol and, in front of it, the restored 1845 Old Capitol with its candy-striped awnings.

item.title: Mission San Luis & the canopy roads
item.blurb: A reconstructed 1600s Spanish-Apalachee mission, then a drive beneath the moss-draped canopy roads.

days.label: Day 245 — Along 30A to Seahaven
days.summary: West down the panhandle, through the town that played a television set.

drive.scenicNote: West and south out of the pines onto US-98, and the Gulf appears on your left for the rest of the day.

item.title: Seahaven — The Truman Show
item.blurb: Seaside was built in the 1980s as an experiment in walkable town-making, and it came out so uncannily perfect that Peter Weir filmed The Truman Show here without building a set. Truman's house is on Natchez Street. Eat from the Airstream food trucks on 30A, walk to the beach pavilions, and enjoy the very slight feeling of being watched.

drive.scenicNote: The rest of 30A and then US-98 along the Emerald Coast — the sand out here is pure quartz washed down from the Appalachians, which is why it's white and squeaks underfoot.
